sections.title: Gradients
sections.question: The three step washes (Publish peach, Test sky, Review mint) and the hero blend, matched to the marketing material, in light and dark, plus card washes and a wash tinted by an uploaded site's own colour (coral, green, navy, yellow examples). Smooth 8-stop fades with a fine grain so they never band.
take: Tokens are generated by make/washes.py; the site wash keeps the site's hue but fixes lightness and strength, so every site stays in the family.

sections.title: Home
sections.question: "What's new" as a plain timeline of events, sites as preview blocks, tests as status lines. Layout A, with the sidebar open and collapsed.
take: Site visits on Home need site analytics (Solo plan); I check we store daily visits before building that event.

sections.title: First run, and only one site or test
sections.question: Every account starts with a personalised sample site ("Mia Chen's very serious portfolio") and a finished test on it, labelled Example and deletable. The first run still teaches Publish, Test, Review.

sections.title: Sites and Tests lists
sections.question: Sites as blocks with a real preview (Live, Private, Free countdown); tests as status lines with a small preview and session dots.

sections.title: Site page
sections.question: Everything on one page: preview, address, drop a new version, versions with roll back; settings (public or private, domain, favicon, badge, name) in a side column. No test push: "User test this site" sits in the site's menu and explains it makes a copy. Private (only people signed in) and Password are separate.

sections.title: Create: one guided flow per source
sections.question: Pick the source first, then its own flow: upload (the wash picks up the site's colours after upload, then "Now test it"), prompt (copy it into Claude or ChatGPT, no connector; blue-dot loader while waiting), Figma link (publish only once the link is checked).

sections.title: Test setup and share
sections.question: Name, optional tasks, welcome and thank-you; optional task descriptions, the link card, "Preview as tester" (recorded as You, free, not in Insights), an open or closed switch for new sessions, the test's own domain and favicon.

sections.title: Tester start screen and task pill
sections.question: Asks for a first name (optional) before any browser prompt, then permissions. The task panel is a square frosted panel the tester can drag aside or minimise, with Done and Couldn't do it, an optional description, and only a small Recording sign (no timer). Light or dark follows the prototype's colour.

sections.title: Sessions
sections.question: One row per tester: name, device, summary or quote, length, tasks 2 of 2, Issue / Confusion / Works well counts with severity, and Watch. "Transcript arriving", "No audio" and "You" rows. New: filters (status, tag, device, audio, tasks, date) and search, plus an All sessions view across tests.

sections.title: Session review: Watch
sections.question: Dark first. Recording left (a recorded tab, no pointer), one timeline with task regions and tag marks plus filter chips, a tidier follow-along transcript (one time column, tags as one quiet line), click to jump, "Back to now", Summary per task, speeds, Skip silence, keyboard sheet, Download menu, previous and next tester.
take: Built on the research: video left and transcript right (UserTesting, Lookback, Grain), one timeline with task and tag markers, Frame.io-style keys.

sections.title: Session review: Read
sections.question: The same session as a calm read: her words as the headline, the summary as the opening, tags and notes in the margin, the video in a corner that keeps playing. One switch between Watch and Read.

sections.title: No tasks, no audio
sections.question: What changes when there are no tasks and no sound: no task lane, an honest "No sound in this recording", Transcript and Read switched off with a reason. Two half-cases beside it.

sections.title: Insights, across sessions
sections.question: Its own tab. Summary first, a score per task, a "Session by session" timeline drawn like the session player (one row per tester from their own start, median, hover to open that moment), issues ranked by severity, then "4 of 6 testers" with playable quote cards, what worked, where testers disagreed, a confidence note. By task, by theme, by priority; Copy as table.

sections.title: Insights: empty and early
sections.question: 0 sessions: three steps say what happens and when, beside a faded Example, with Copy test link and Open the example. 2 sessions: "Patterns appear from 3 sessions", low confidence, "Seen so far".

sections.title: Marketing versions
sections.question: The real components, bigger and simpler, and a homepage hero and a social card built only from them.

tiles.label: Make team: site block, test link card, what's-new rows, hero
Review team: session row, quote card, player, social card

intro: Round v3: v2 polished with your notes and your 16 answers. ink buttons with quiet glass, "Aero." in Geist with the blue dot, dark mode, Sites and Tests separate with "Test this site" making a copy, testers with names, one guided flow per source, and the review screens built on the research into pro tools (Lookback, UserTesting, Grain, Maze, Dovetail, Frame.io).
Two teams, one shared stylesheet, so it reads as one product. Every screen is shown in light and then dark. Mark each screen Keep, Parts of it or Drop, with a note; I read the marks before building.
The questions that need your answer are at the bottom.
roles: sites, tests, insights as its own tab
patterns: A moving cursor in a replay
recommend: Private means: only people in your workspace (drawn), or any signed-in person you invite?
The site-tinted wash: read automatically from the site's screenshot (drawn), or picked by you?
Sample site copy and address: "Hello. This is my very serious portfolio. Mostly serious." at mia-chen-example.aeroapp.ai. Right tone?
Tester task panel: remember the corner the tester last moved it to?
All sessions: a tab on the Tests page (drawn) or its own item in the sidebar?
Settled from the pricing facts, no answer needed: custom favicon is Basic and up, custom domain on tests Solo and up.
I still check in the code before building: task ticks with times, tasks counting with no audio, skipping silence, and stored daily site visits.
